Rashi on Chullin 15a:12:1.hebrew: כי מורי להו רב לתלמידיה - במבשל בשבת, הוראה ביחיד, מורי להו כרבי מאיר דמיקל:
Rashi on Chullin 15a:12:1.english: When Rav taught it to his students - Regarding one who cooks on Shabbat, since this was a ruling given privately [to an individual], he taught them like Rabbi Meir, who is lenient.

Rashi on Chullin 15a:12:2.english: At his lecture - On Shabbat, in public.

Rashi on Chullin 15a:13:1.hebrew: וכי תימא תנא בפירקיה תנא קמיה - ברבים היה שונה משנה זו ביום הדרשה, וחייש רב לעמי הארץ שלא ישמעו קולו:
Rashi on Chullin 15a:13:1.english: And if you would say: He taught it in his lecture, [and] a tanna [recited it] before him - [Rav] would teach this mishna in public on the day of his lecture, and Rav was concerned for the common people, who would not be able to hear his voice [directly, so a reciter would repeat his words aloud for the benefit of those in the back].

Rashi on Chullin 15a:13:2.english: Is that to say - [The word "everyone" refers to] the members of the congregation who would come to hear what Rav was expounding.

Rashi on Chullin 15a:13:3.english: They listen to a reciter - That is to say, they incline their ear to hear from the students sitting there, who each recite his own teaching to himself.

Rashi on Chullin 15a:13:4.english: To the amora - who would stand before the Rav and announce to the public what the head of the lecture would whisper to him; it was to him that they would listen.

Rashi on Chullin 15a:14:1.hebrew: עד כאן לא קשרי ר"מ אלא במבשל - בשוגג, דכיון דאיסור שבת ליכא דשוגג הוא, איסור מוקצה נמי ליכא, דמעיקרא הוי חזי לכוס חיה:
Rashi on Chullin 15a:14:1.english: Up to this point, Rabbi Meir only permits [eating] in the case of one who cooked - [This is referring to a case done] unwittingly. Since there is no violation of the Shabbat prohibition - because it was inadvertent - the prohibition of muktzeh also does not apply, for beforehand [the meat] was already fit for an animal to chew, [i.e., to be eaten raw].

Rashi on Chullin 15a:14:2.hebrew: אבל שוחט - בשוגג, נהי דאיסור שבת ליכא, משום מוקצה מיהא אסורה, דבין השמשות לא הויא חזיא לכוס. כל אכילה שלא כדרכה קרי כוסס, כמו (ברכות דף לז.) הכוסס את החיטין, הכוסס את האורז, כס פילפלי ביומא דכפורי (שם דף לו:):
Rashi on Chullin 15a:14:2.english: But one who slaughters - Unwittingly: Granted that there is no violation of the Shabbat prohibition [in such a case], nevertheless it is forbidden on account of muktzeh, since at twilight [before Shabbat began, the animal, being alive,] was not fit to be eaten raw. Any eating that is not in its normal manner is called "koses" (gnawing/chewing), as in (Berakhot 37a): "one who chews wheat kernels," "one who chews rice," [and] "he chewed pepper on Yom Kippur" (ibid. 36b).

Rashi on Chullin 15a:15:1.hebrew: הא ר"מ שרי - מדאיצטריך לאוקמה כרבי יהודה, מכלל דקסבר רב דר"מ שרי:
Rashi on Chullin 15a:15:1.english: But Rabbi Meir permits - Since it was necessary to establish it [the mishna] in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, this implies that Rav holds that Rabbi Meir permits [it].

Rashi on Chullin 15a:1:1.hebrew: כל הנרות של מתכת מטלטלים - דשל מתכות לא מאיסי אפילו ישנים, כגון של נחושת וכיוצא בהן:
Rashi on Chullin 15a:1:1.english: All metal lamps may be handled - Because metal [lamps] are not repulsive even when old, such as those of copper and the like.

Rashi on Chullin 15a:1:2.hebrew: הדולק בשבת - שהיה נר דולק בו בין השמשות, דמוקצה מחמת איסור שאסור לכבות הנר, נאסר גם הוא לטלטל, וכיון שהוקצה לבין השמשות, הוקצה לכל היום:
Rashi on Chullin 15a:1:2.english: The one burning on Shabbat - [Meaning,] a lamp was burning in it during twilight, which is muktzeh machmat issur (set aside due to a prohibition), since it is forbidden to extinguish the lamp; it, too, becomes forbidden to move. And since it was set aside for twilight, it was set aside for the entire day.

Rashi on Chullin 15a:2:1.hebrew: בידים - שהדליקו בו הנר, אבל בהמה דממילא מידחיא, אימר דהדר חזיא:
Rashi on Chullin 15a:2:1.english: By hand - That they lit the lamp with it [actively rendering it unfit]. But an animal that becomes disqualified on its own, one might say that it reverts to being fit.

Rashi on Chullin 15a:3:1.hebrew: יאכל - הוא עצמו ובו ביום, ואין צריך להמתין עד הערב בכדי שיעשו, דהא דאמרינן בעלמא לערב בכדי שיעשו לית ליה לר"מ, אלא היכא דעבד ישראל איסורא ובמזיד, דאיכא חיובא דלא נמטייה הנאה מאיסורא, אבל בשוגג לא:
Rashi on Chullin 15a:3:1.english: It may be eaten - The [food] itself, and on that very day, and there is no need to wait until evening for the amount of time it would take to prepare it. For that which we say elsewhere, [that one must wait] "until evening, the time it takes to prepare it," Rabbi Meir does not hold by, except where a Jew committed the transgression, and intentionally, since there is an obligation not to let him derive benefit from the transgression; but where it was unwitting - not so.

Rashi on Chullin 15a:3:2.english: Intentionally - [Meaning,] where there is a prohibition [i.e., he knew it was Shabbat and that cooking was forbidden].

Rashi on Chullin 15a:3:3.hebrew: לא יאכל - בו ביום עד שתחשך ובכדי שיעשו. והוא הדין לאחרים נמי דאסור למיכליה בו ביום, דטעמא משום דלא נמטייה הנאה מאיסורא הוא, וכי שהי לאורתא בכדי שיעשו לא מטי לו הנאה מיניה. ואיידי דתנא רישא בדידיה, דאשמעינן רבותא להתירא, תנא נמי סיפא בדידיה:
Rashi on Chullin 15a:3:3.english: He may not eat [it] - on that day, until it gets dark, and [only after] enough time has passed that it could have been done [prepared in the normal way]. And the same is true for others as well - that it is forbidden for them to eat it on that day - because the reason [for the prohibition] is so that he should not derive benefit from a transgression; and when he waits until evening, for the amount of time it would take to be done, benefit does not reach him from it. And since the first clause taught [the law] with regard to him [the one who slaughtered], to teach us the novelty of the leniency [that he himself may eventually eat it], the latter clause was also taught with regard to him.

Rashi on Chullin 15a:4:1.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר בשוגג יאכל במוצאי שבת - ולא בשבת. וה"ה לאחריני, דאע"ג דבשוגג חיוב סקילה ליכא, עבירה מיהא איכא, ובעינן בכדי שיעשו דלא נימטיה הנאה מעבירה. ואיידי דבעי למתני סיפא "לא יאכל עולמית" בדידיה, אבל לאחריני שרי - דאיהו דעבד איסורא קנסוהו רבנן, אבל אחריני לא - תנא רישא נמי בדידיה. ומתניתין נמי דקתני "אסורה באכילה ליומיה", לדידיה ולאחריני, בשוגג מתוקמא ורבי יהודה היא. ולקמן פריך: והא "מתחייב בנפשו" קתני! והא ליכא למימר רישא נמי דוקא איהו, אבל אחריני שרו בו ביום, ואיהו אסור משום דקנסו שוגג אטו מזיד, ומתניתין דאסר ליה ליומיה אפילו לאחריני לאו רבי יהודה היא - דא"כ דקנסא דרישא אטו מזיד הוא, אמאי מישתרי הוא לאורתא? הא קתני גבי מזיד "לא יאכל עולמית"! אלא טעמא משום דלא ליתהני מעבירה הוא, ולא שנא הוא ולא שנא אחריני:
Rashi on Chullin 15a:4:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: If done unwittingly, he may eat it after Shabbat - But not on Shabbat itself. And the same applies to others [besides the one who cooked]: even though in the case of an unwitting act there is no liability of stoning, there is nevertheless a transgression, and we require [waiting] the time it takes to prepare it, so that he not benefit from a transgression. And since [the Tanna] wanted to teach in the latter clause, "he may never eat it," referring to himself - while for others it is permitted, because the Rabbis penalized the one who committed the forbidden act, but not others - he therefore taught the first clause also with reference to himself. And the Mishnah too, which states "it is forbidden to eat it that day," referring both to himself and to others, is speaking of an unwitting act and follows Rabbi Yehuda. And later [the Gemara] raises a difficulty: but it teaches "he is liable for his life" [which implies a deliberate act]! And one cannot say that the first clause is also specifically about him alone - while others are permitted to eat it on that same day, and he himself is forbidden because they penalized the unwitting act on account of the deliberate one - and that the Mishnah, which forbids it for that day even to others, does not follow Rabbi Yehuda. For if so, that the penalty in the first clause is imposed on account of a deliberate act, why is he himself permitted to eat it in the evening? It teaches, regarding a deliberate act, "he may never eat it"! Rather, the reason [for the prohibition on that day] is that he should not benefit from a transgression - and it makes no difference whether it is himself or others.

Rashi on Chullin 15a:5:2.hebrew: במזיד לא יאכל עולמית כו' - לאו משום קנסא הוא, דהא אחריני לא עבוד איסורא, אלא מקראי יליף לה רבי יוחנן בכתובות באלו נערות (כתובות דף לד:) ובב"ק בפרק מרובה (בבא קמא דף עא.): ושמרתם את השבת כי קדש וגו', מה קדש אסור באכילה אף מעשה שבת אסורים באכילה, יכול אפילו בשוגג, ת"ל מחלליה מות יומת, במזיד אמרתי ולא בשוגג:
Rashi on Chullin 15a:5:2.english: If done intentionally, he may never eat it, etc. - This is not on account of a penalty, for the others did not commit any transgression; rather, Rabbi Yochanan derives it from verses, in [tractate] Ketubot, in [the chapter] Elu Ne'arot (Ketubot 34b), and in Bava Kamma, in the chapter Merubah (Bava Kamma 71a): "And you shall keep the Sabbath, for it is holy to you," etc. - just as [that which is] holy is forbidden to eat, so too the product of [forbidden] work [done] on the Sabbath is forbidden to eat. [One might think] this applies even [if it was done] unwittingly - the verse states, "Whoever desecrates it shall be put to death" - I spoke [that verse] of one who acted intentionally, and not unwittingly.

Rashi on Chullin 15a:6:1.english: And let us establish it as referring to a case of intentional [transgression], and it follows Rabbi Meir - Who says that it is forbidden [only] for that day.

Rashi on Chullin 15a:7:1.english: Just as Yom Kippur, etc. - [Just as] one may not eat on that day, since it is a day of affliction [fasting].

Rashi on Chullin 15a:9:1.hebrew: ונוקמה כר' יוחנן הסנדלר דאמר כו' - לא יאכל בו ביום, לא הוא ולא אחרים. ואית דמפרשי דהאי במזיד לא יאכל דרבי מאיר, ובשוגג לא יאכל דרבי יהודה, לא יאכל הוא, אבל לאחרים שרי, והאי אסורה באכילה ליומיה דקאמר רב נמי לדידיה קאמר, אבל לאחריני שרי, ולאו מילתא, דהא דומיא דיום הכפורים קתני, דלא שנא לו ולא שנא לאחרים אסור, ועוד אסורה באכילה ליומא לגמרי משמע:
Rashi on Chullin 15a:9:1.english: And let us establish it in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar, who says, etc. - [The verse] "he shall not eat it on that day" [means] neither he himself nor others [may eat it]. And there are those who explain that "intentionally, he shall not eat" is [the ruling of] Rabbi Meir, and "unwittingly, he shall not eat" is [the ruling of] Rabbi Yehuda - [meaning] he himself may not eat it, but for others it is permitted; and this [phrase], "it is forbidden to eat on that day," which Rav states, is likewise stated only with regard to himself, but for others it is permitted. But this is not correct, for it is taught here in a manner similar to Yom Kippur, where it makes no difference - whether for himself or for others, it is forbidden. Moreover, "it is forbidden to eat" implies that it is entirely forbidden that day [to everyone].

Tosafot on Chullin 15a:12:1.hebrew: מורי להו כר"מ - משמע שכן הלכה, וכן דרש רבא בפ' כירה (שבת דף לח. ע"ש) כר"מ. וקשה מכאן לפי' הקונטרס, דבריש אין צדין (ביצה דף כד:) גבי עובד כוכבים שהביא דורון לישראל, אם יש מאותו המין במחובר אסורין, ולערב נמי אסורין בכדי שיעשו, ופירש הקונט' דטעמא דאסורין בכדי שיעשו כדי שלא יהנה ממלאכת י"ט; והרי מבשל בשבת דבשוגג יאכל, אע"ג דנהנה ממלאכת שבת! ומיהו י"ל דאין נהנה כ"כ, כיון דבלאו בישול ראוי לכוס. אבל קשה משוחט בשבת בשוגג דיאכל לר"מ, היכא דהיה לו חולה מבעוד יום והבריא, כדאמרינן בסמוך, משום דלא הוי מוקצה, ולא אסר מטעם שנהנה ממלאכת שבת. וי"ל דבמילתא דלא שכיח לא גזרו:
Tosafot on Chullin 15a:12:1.english: They taught it like R. Meir - This implies that such is the halacha, and Rava likewise taught, in the chapter "Kirah" (Shabbat 38a, see there), like R. Meir. And this is difficult from here for Rashi's commentary, at the beginning of [the chapter] "Ein Tzadin" (Beitzah 24b), regarding a gentile who brought a gift to a Jew: if there is [produce] of that species still attached [to the ground elsewhere], it is forbidden; and even in the evening [after the festival], it remains forbidden for as long as it would take to prepare it (be-khedei she-ya'asu). And Rashi explained that the reason it is forbidden for that duration is so that he should not benefit from labor done on Yom Tov; but behold, [in the case of] one who cooks on Shabbat unwittingly, [the food] may be eaten [right away], even though he benefits from the labor of Shabbat! However, one can say that he does not benefit so much [from the cooking], since even without cooking it would be fit to be chewed [i.e., eaten raw]. But it is difficult from [the case of] one who slaughters on Shabbat unwittingly, that [the meat] may be eaten, according to R. Meir, in a case where he had a sick person [who needed it] from before Shabbat and [the sick person] recovered - as we say shortly - because it was not muktzeh, and he did not forbid it on the grounds that he benefits from the labor of Shabbat. And one can say that in a matter that is not common, they did not enact a decree.

Tosafot on Chullin 15a:16:1.hebrew: כי שרי ר"מ כגון שהיה לו חולה מבעוד יום - וא"ת, ונוקי מתניתין בשוגג ור"מ, ולא היה לו חולה כלל; וי"ל, דדומיא דיוה"כ קתני, דאסור אף על גב דהיה לו חולה. וא"ת, והא על כרחיך לא הוה לגמרי דומיא דיוה"כ, דבשבת אם לא הבריא מותר אפי' לרבי יהודה; וי"ל, דבמקום ששייך חיוב קא מדמה שבת ליוה"כ, כדתני אע"פ שמתחייב בנפשו:
Tosafot on Chullin 15a:16:1.english: When R. Meir permits [it], it is where he had a sick person [needing to eat] while it was still day [before Shabbat began] - And if you say: let us establish the Mishnah as referring to an unwitting act, and [following] R. Meir, and there was no sick person at all; one can answer: it teaches [a case] similar to Yom Kippur, that it is forbidden even though he had a sick person. And if you say: but perforce it cannot be completely similar to Yom Kippur, for on Shabbat, if [the sick person] did not recover, it is permitted even according to R. Yehuda; one can answer: where liability applies, [the Mishnah] likens Shabbat to Yom Kippur, as it teaches, "even though he is liable for his life."

Tosafot on Chullin 15a:3:1.hebrew: המבשל בשבת בשוגג יאכל - אפילו בו ביום, דר"מ לא קניס כלל שוגג אטו מזיד, כדמוכח בהניזקין (גיטין נג:). ובפ' כירה (שבת דף לח.) נמי משמע דשרי בו ביום, גבי הא דבעי מרבי חייא בר אבא: שכח קדירה ע"ג כירה כו', במזיד לא יאכל לא הוא ולא אחרים בו ביום, אבל במוצ"ש שרי אפי' לדידיה - מדבעי לאוקמי מתניתין ר"מ ובמזיד, ומתניתין דומיא דיוה"כ קתני דאסור בו ביום בין לו בין לאחרים, ושחיטתו כשרה קתני לא שנא לו ולא שנא לאחרים, כדאמרינן בסמוך. ועוד, אי במזיד לא יאכל עולמית לר"מ, א"כ היינו מזיד דרבי יהודה, כמו שאפרש; וכן שוגג דרבי יהודה, דהא מוקי מתניתין בשוגג ורבי יהודה, ובמזיד לא יאכל עולמית הוא, אבל אחרים אוכלים למוצאי שבת - דאי לא יאכלו עולמית, א"כ היינו מזיד דרבי יוחנן הסנדלר. ועוד, דבמרובה (ב"ק דף עא.) מוקי דרבנן דפטרו בטבח בשבת מתשלומי ד' וה' כרבי יוחנן הסנדלר, ולא מוקי לה כר' יהודה; ובעי נמי התם מאי טעמא דר' יוחנן הסנדלר, ולא בעי מ"ט דר' יהודה. כללא דמילתא: מזיד דר"מ שוגג דר' יהודה, מזיד דרבי יהודה שוגג דרבי יוחנן הסנדלר:
Tosafot on Chullin 15a:3:1.english: One who cooks on Shabbat unwittingly may eat [it] - Even on that [same] day - for R' Meir did not penalize the unwitting [transgressor] at all on account of [confusion with] the intentional [transgressor] - as is proven in [the chapter] "Ha-Nizakin" (Gittin 53b). And in the chapter "Kirah" (Shabbat 38a) too it is implied that it is permitted on that day, regarding the question that was asked of Rabbi Chiya bar Abba: "He forgot a pot on the stove, etc." - if [it was done] intentionally, neither he nor others may eat it on that day, but on Motzaei Shabbat it is permitted even for him [himself] - since [the Gemara] wants to establish the Mishnah as [following] R' Meir and referring to an intentional [transgression], and the Mishnah teaches [the law as] similar to Yom Kippur, that it is forbidden on that day both for him and for others, while "its slaughter is valid" is taught without distinguishing between him and others, as we shall say shortly. Furthermore, if according to R' Meir he may never eat it for an intentional [transgression], then this would be the same as an intentional [transgression] according to R' Yehuda, as I shall explain; and likewise [the same would hold for] an unwitting [transgression] according to R' Yehuda - for [the Gemara] establishes the Mishnah as referring to an unwitting [transgression] and [the view of] R' Yehuda, and for an intentional [transgression] he himself may never eat it, but others eat it on Motzaei Shabbat - for if they too may never eat it, then this would be the same as an intentional [transgression] according to R' Yochanan HaSandlar. Furthermore, in [the chapter] "Merubah" (Bava Kamma 71a), [the Gemara] establishes that the Rabbis who exempt one who slaughters [an animal] on Shabbat from the fourfold and fivefold payment follow R' Yochanan HaSandlar, and does not establish it according to R' Yehuda; and there [the Gemara] also asks what is the reason for R' Yochanan HaSandlar's view, but does not ask the reason for R' Yehuda's view. The general rule of the matter: an intentional [transgression] according to R' Meir [is equivalent to] an unwitting [transgression] according to R' Yehuda; an intentional [transgression] according to R' Yehuda [is equivalent to] an unwitting [transgression] according to R' Yochanan HaSandlar.

Rashi on Chullin 15a:5:1.hebrew: ר' יוחנן הסנדלר אומר בשוגג יאכל למוצאי שבת - בכדי שיעשו, כר' יהודה דמשוי ליה עבירה אף בשוגג, ועדיפא מדרבי יהודה, דאילו רבי יהודה שרי ליה לאורתא אפי' לדידיה דלא קניס שוגג אטו מזיד, ורבי יוחנן קניס שוגג אטו מזיד, הלכך איהו דעבד איסורא קנסו רבנן, אחריני דלא עבדי איסורא לא קנסו, אלא בכדי שיעשו ימתינו, דלא ניתהני מעבירה:
Rashi on Chullin 15a:5:1.english: R' Yochanan HaSandlar says: If [it was cooked] unwittingly, he may eat it at the conclusion of Shabbos - [Meaning,] enough time [must pass] for it to be prepared [anew], following Rabbi Yehuda, who treats it as a transgression even when done unwittingly - and [this ruling] is even more stringent than Rabbi Yehuda's. For Rabbi Yehuda permits it that very evening, even to the one who cooked it himself, since he does not penalize an unwitting act on account of a deliberate one; whereas Rabbi Yochanan does penalize an unwitting act on account of a deliberate one. Therefore: the one who committed the transgression - the Rabbis penalized him; others who did not commit the transgression - they were not penalized, except that they must wait the time it takes to prepare it, so that they not benefit from the transgression.
